subject: Marketplace private offer pricing qualification for BrightCart (post-call)
messages:

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Marketplace private offer pricing qualification for BrightCart (post-call)

Hi Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- BrightCart priority: integrate Redwood for both real-time chat generation and batch embeddings (search).
- Estimated monthly token volume (you mentioned a range): 50M – 120M tokens/month.
- Budget guidance: you indicated a target spend range of roughly $60k – $125k / month while you scale.
- Procurement preference: AWS Marketplace Private Offer (you confirmed procurement wants to go through Marketplace PO).
- Key ask for us: confirm target net unit economics (target $/1M tokens to BrightCart) and the token mix (percent real-time generation vs embeddings).

Next steps: 
1) If you can confirm the exact preferred target $ / 1M tokens (a target range is fine), we will map that to an AWS Marketplace list price and produce a PO-ready private offer draft.
2) Please share the procurement contact + PO template (if different from what you already sent).
3) We'll include an example unit-price mapping and expected invoice flow (AWS invoice -> Marketplace fee applied -> Redwood receives net).

I've attached our preliminary pricing sheet so you can see how we map SKUs to tokens.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing qualification for BrightCart (post-call)

Thanks Marissa — good notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed token volumes: we expect ~75M tokens/mo initially, with a high-growth plan to 150M tokens/mo over 3–6 months. Peak day could be ~10% of monthly.
- Token mix: 70% real-time generation (chat) / 30% embeddings (batch).
- Target net unit economics to BrightCart (what we want to pay): $7 – $9 per 1M tokens (net to vendor).
- Procurement contact: procurement@brightcart.com (attachment: brightcart_po_template.pdf).
- Marketplace: prefer AWS Private Offer; Dave Huang (cc'd) is our AWS Marketplace rep.

If you can send a mapping that shows (a) Redwood list/unit price on AWS Marketplace, (b) marketplace fee %, (c) resulting net/unit to Redwood, that'll help speed up the PO. Also need expected billing cadence (monthly) and any minimum commitment options to lower unit price.

— Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Partnerships | BrightCart
samir@brightcart.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightcart.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Dave Huang <dave.huang@aws-partner.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer pricing qualification for BrightCart (post-call)

Great — thanks for the details, Samir. Internal note (cc'ing Aditya and Neha to align on Marketplace mapping).

High-level: AWS Marketplace Private Offers require us to set a list price (what shows on AWS invoice); AWS will apply a marketplace fee (typically a percentage) so the net Redwood receives is the list price less that fee. Below is an example mapping based on your target net of $7 – $9 / 1M tokens.

Example unit-price mapping (illustrative):
- Target net to Redwood: $7.00 / 1M tokens
- AWS Marketplace fee (example): 10%
- Required AWS list price = net / (1 - fee) = 7.00 / 0.90 = $7.78 / 1M tokens

Similarly for $9 net: 9.00 / 0.90 = $10.00 / 1M tokens (rounded).

We also typically map separate SKUs for: 
- Real-time generation (per-1M tokens, streaming eligible)
- Embeddings (per-1M tokens)
- Reserved commit SKUs (if you want lower unit prices for a monthly committed spend)

To answer your specific asks: 
- Billing cadence: monthly invoice through AWS (standard).
- Commitment options: we can offer a tiered reserved-price table (e.g., 3-month or 12-month commit) to reduce net unit price – we'll include those tiers in the pricing sheet.
- Minimums: none required to start; we can propose optional committed tiers.

Action items from us: 
1) We'll produce a PO-ready AWS Private Offer mapping showing the AWS list price per SKU, the marketplace fee %, and the resulting net price to Redwood (example math above).
2) We'll include a recommended mapping given your 70/30 mix and expected 75M starting volume.
3) Please confirm whether you prefer a single blended SKU or separate SKUs for generation vs embeddings (separate SKUs recommended).

I'm attaching an updated pricing sheet with the example math and tiered commit options. We'll aim to have a draft private-offer proposal for procurement in 2–3 business days once you confirm the SKU preference.

Thanks –
Marissa
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.xlsx

3) Attach SOC2 & security attestation links and an onboarding SOW (brief).
4) Schedule a 30-min procurement review with Samir + procurement on 2026-12-03 to sign off on PO wording.

I'm attaching the pricing sheet and an AWS private-offer FAQ for your team to review. Let me know if you need anything else before the draft – we want to make the procurement review as frictionless as possible.
